neighbours.label: a conversational aside or interjection that interrupts a sentence ('Well,' after a question, 'ahem', 'you know,'), as against the same sentences said straight
fire: Do I like the new boss? Well, that is a complicated question.
His speech was, ahem, slightly longer than the ten minutes he promised.
We spent the whole night with, you know, the usual crowd from work.
Can we finish this by Friday? Well, that depends on the printer.
The cake she brought was, ahem, not entirely homemade.
She ended up dating, you know, the guy from the coffee shop.
Is the hotel close to the beach? Well, close is a relative word.
My brother's driving is, ahem, an acquired taste.
quiet: I do not like the new boss, because the job is a complicated one.
His speech was slightly longer than the ten minutes he promised.
We spent the whole night with the usual crowd from work.
We can finish this by Friday if the printer works.
The cake she brought was not entirely homemade.
She ended up dating the guy from the coffee shop.
The hotel is close to the beach and has a large pool.
My brother drives an old blue truck to his job.

predictions: fire 0.25-0.55 on the interjection or the comma around it; straight versions below 0.2. Broad weak pole, may fail.
